## 2. Election Column References (Section 1.6.2)

**Problem:** The `transmute()` block references columns by positional names (`...47`, `...35`, `...59`, `...53`) generated by `read_excel`. A grader reading the code cannot tell which candidate these correspond to without opening the Excel file themselves. This hurts the "easy to follow" and "well-commented" criteria.

**Location:** Section 1.6.2, around lines 95–105 (the `election_dept <- election_raw |> transmute(...)` block).

**Fix:** Add a comment block above the `transmute()` explaining the column mapping. Example:

```r
# The XLSX has repeating column groups per candidate. read_excel assigns
# positional names (...N) to the unnamed "% Voix/Exp" columns.
# Mapping (verified against the raw header row):
#   ...35 = Macron  (% Voix/Exp)
#   ...47 = Le Pen  (% Voix/Exp)
#   ...53 = Zemmour (% Voix/Exp)
#   ...59 = Mélenchon (% Voix/Exp)
```

**Validation:** After adding the comment, no code changes needed — just verify the script still runs through Section 1.6 without error.

## 3. Update Hardcoded Values (Section 5.2.6)

**Problem:** The "after" values in the income impact table (Section 5.2.6) are pulled dynamically from `all_results`, so they now reflect the post-fix XGBoost numbers (R²=0.670 instead of 0.679). The "before" values are hardcoded and remain correct. No code change needed, but verify the printed output looks right — the XGBoost R² gain will now show +0.071 instead of +0.080.

**Task:** Run Section 5.2.6 and confirm the table prints without errors and the numbers are internally consistent.
